summary: The issue root-cause section states the rules-corpus source freeze is inherent to the pin design and latent since the pin was created; both claims are false. The ancestry precondition that creates the freeze was introduced four days earlier by one commit.
evidence: command:git log --oneline -S require_durable_source_commit -- scripts/verify-rules-corpus.sh (returns only d76b477 and d1f6ea7); command:git merge-base --is-ancestor 902ac733 origin/main (exits non-zero, so the pin immediately preceding d76b477 was a feature-branch head and would fail the check that commit added); issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#264
cost: One full design cycle built and reverted: a two-set membership redesign of implementation-sources.json plus verify-rules-corpus.sh, abandoned after the intent read contradicted the premise.
owner: S.I.R. / issue triage for board rows whose root-cause section is authored before the authoring history is read

summary: No document in the repository states a membership criterion for the 19 paths in implementation-sources.json. The architecture doc, the single ADR, the rules-manifest contract, every work package, and both rules skills are silent, and the most recent work item calls them the intended normalized implementation sources without saying what makes them intended.
cost: Membership had to be reconstructed from commit archaeology and feedback prose rather than read; this is the gap that made narrowing the set look defensible.

summary: The durability hardening added four inversions proving its refusals fire, but none proving the rebind path it constrains still had a legal execution. The precondition it introduced cannot be satisfied by any pull request that changes a pinned source, and nothing detected that because no pull request had changed one since.
cost: Six board rows blocked: S.I.R.#249 and S.I.R.#232 directly, and #230, #233, #234, #235, #236 behind #232.
owner: S.I.R. / scripts/verify-rules-corpus.sh, and more generally any gate adding a precondition without an inversion that its satisfying path remains reachable

evidence: command:grep -rl implementation-sources scripts/ src/ tests/ (all five hits are readers; scripts/generate-rules-corpus.sh has none); file:src/SIR.Simulation/CombatRules.fs; file:scripts/verify-rules-corpus.sh

owner: S.I.R. / scripts, a --rebind or --write mode for the implementation source manifest and its sealed digest

summary: The review-wait receipt field claimGeneration is the claim marker COMMENT ID, not the renewed= value carried inside that marker body. Both are long numerals on the same comment, so the wrong one looks correct, and the refusal names neither.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord review wait S.I.R.#264 event.json --pr 276 (refused with: receipt claimGeneration is not current, when given renewed=639230392768239071; accepted when given the comment id 5383131140); issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#255
cost: One refused round trip and a reflection pass over FS.GG.Coord.Core.dll that found no producer function for the value, because it is not derived in the assembly at all.
owner: FS-GG Coordination Kit / review wait refusal text should name the field source, as the landable refusal was asked to name its producing command

summary: An initial review wait must be entered at round 0. Round 1 is accepted and durably appended by review wait, then rejected afterwards by the review oracle as unauthorized, so the invalid state is written before it is diagnosed.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord review S.I.R.#264 --pr 276 (the durable review wait does not authorize dispatchCritic: expected generation ...:initial-review:0, got ...:initial-review:1); command:scripts/fsgg-coord review wait S.I.R.#264 enter-round-1.json --pr 276 (accepted, commentId 5383246998)
cost: One wasted entry plus a cancel event on a digest-sealed append-only ledger; three comments where one was needed.
owner: FS-GG Coordination Kit / review wait should validate the round against the protocol state at append time rather than accepting an entry the oracle will refuse

summary: Deriving the review-wait document with the engine own ReviewWait.generationToken and ReviewWait.encode, rather than hand-writing JSON, produced a document accepted on its first structurally valid attempt and surfaced the required-field rule through ReviewWait.validate before any board write.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi over FS.GG.Coord.Core.dll calling ReviewWait.validate then ReviewWait.encode (validate reported claimGeneration is required locally, with no network round trip)
owner: FS-GG Coordination Kit / worth documenting as the supported way to author wait and record drafts

summary: Acceptance evidence that confirms the thesis is not adversarial evidence. Two instances by one agent: an acceptance demonstration that mutated a declared rule fact the sibling check already refused, so it measured the sibling rather than the mechanism under test; and a CI diagnosis that fitted this item's own defect class and was adopted without checking the one fact that falsifies it. A third instance followed: the critic's verdict marker was acted on without opening the review, so one of its two findings went unread.
evidence: issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#264; command:gh api repos/EHotwagner/S.I.R./issues/276/comments --jq '.[] | select(.id==5383452179) | .body'; command:gh run view 32607930272 --repo EHotwagner/S.I.R. --json attempt --jq .attempt
cost: One material review finding requiring a repair round, one refuted CI diagnosis, one withdrawn host relay.

summary: The review verdict and the review findings are two separate PR comments, and acting on the first without opening the second left half a changes-required verdict unrepaired. The sealed fsgg:review-decision/v2 marker carries the verdict, route applicability and route evidence but no finding bodies; the findings arrived three minutes later in a separate comment containing two of them.
evidence: command:gh api repos/EHotwagner/S.I.R./issues/276/comments --jq (.[] | select(.id==5383444833) | .body) is the sealed verdict with no findings; the same query for id 5383452179 is the 23515-character review carrying M1 and M2; command:git show --stat bf2b93afed5291a664baec0c36d60cb335660abf shows the first repair round addressing M1 only
cost: One repair round that believed itself complete while M2 was unread, and whose M1 fix replaced one fixed build project with another and so would not have fixed M2 either.
owner: FS-GG Coordination Kit / the review record could name its findings comment, or the oracle could report the finding count with resumeImplementer

summary: A guard added specifically to prove a new check could fail was itself unable to fail, twelve lines above a correct sibling. The inject-combat-divergence arm computes its offset with Array.findIndex, which throws when the two evaluations agree, then failwiths regardless, so the process aborts whether or not a divergence exists and an exit-code-only assertion passes in both worlds. The sibling arm asserts the divergence diagnostic; this one omitted it.
evidence: file:tests/SIR.Conformance.Shared/Program.fs; file:scripts/verify-rules-corpus.sh; command:sed -i 110s/CombatFixtures.evaluate true/CombatFixtures.evaluate false/ tests/SIR.Conformance.Shared/Program.fs then bash scripts/verify-rules-corpus.sh (exit 0 before the repair, exit 1 after with combat divergence mutation failed without the actionable divergence diagnostic)
cost: One review round; the defect was introduced while repairing a gate whose subject is checks that cannot fail.
owner: S.I.R. / gate-authoring convention: an inversion must be observed failing with its subject deliberately broken, not only passing with the subject intact
